title: Mixed-cup TensorNormalization
statement:
Fix the stages, tensors and scalar changes of [def-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-data] and the field coordinates of [def-sf-mixed-cup-field-normalization]. Define six elementary tensor-normalization predicates. For an arbitrary finite-ring homomorphism the tensor comparison, conjugated by the recorded tensor functor equalities and the finite model isomorphisms [def-pur-finite-pullback-tensor-comparison], is the unique ringed derived balancing tensor comparison [def-sf-compact-support-scalar-tensor-identification]. For a completed integral inclusion it is the recorded integral tensor scalar comparison, and for a finite-field inclusion it is the recorded rational tensor scalar comparison [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

For integral reduction require, on every pair of good flat K-flat integral representatives [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex] and their isomorphisms to the two inputs, equality to the actual integral-tensor finite-comparison map [def-sf-integral-tensor-finite-comparison] induced by the recorded Roos projection, inserting the two canonical reduction-model identifications and the finite K-flat tensor-model comparison [def-sf-operation-stages]. The reductions of good representatives are flat K-flat representatives. For rationalization the raw localized tensor-object comparison is the identity, with its fixed equality transports. For closure use the inverse common-stage tensor comparison of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] represented at the input finite field, with the normalized scalar unitors and the recorded common tensor object equation. These three specifications include equality transports; they do not leave any tensor isomorphism arbitrary. All field-point scalar identifications are those of [def-sf-mixed-cup-field-coordinates]. The separately named elementary and closure predicates are those of [def-sf-mixed-cup-tensor-elementary]. The separately named elementary and closure predicates are those of [def-sf-mixed-cup-tensor-closure].

proof.text: For reducedGood, view the specified unrestricted finite reduction as the additive change-of-rings functor along the completed coefficient projection. Its defining existence witness gives its object and morphism equations. Convert flatness of each integral term from the site-sheaf tensor presentation to the monoidal tensor presentation using siteSheafTensorRightIso. Apply changeOfRings_isKFlat_of_flat_terms_independentCoefficients to P.property. Convert the resulting independent K-flat predicate to IsAcyclicTensorKFlat at the common universe u+1, and convert termwise exactness back through siteSheafTensorRightIso. Pair the two conclusions. The two normalization predicates and their prescribed maps are unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0G7E, coefficient-change case; specialization of the existing independent-universe change-of-rings theorem.
